Submit your questions on Canvas by Sunday 9/20 at 11:59 pm, before Monday's class.

## Assigned

1. Chapter 4 of @coles_extremes:2001, "Threshold Models", pages 74--84.

    - Section 4.1 (p. 74): useful introduction
    - Section 4.2 (pp. 75--78): follow the argument, it's OK if you skim the math
    - Section 4.3 (pp. 78--84): most important. Threshold choice in 4.3.1, parameter estimation in 4.3.2, and return levels in 4.3.3.
    - Section 4.4: optional examples. If you read any of it, read the daily rainfall example in 4.4.1

1. Section 5.3 of @coles_extremes:2001, "Modeling Stationary Series", pages 97--100.

1. Part IV of the HEC "Extreme Value Theory" series (slides 34--48), which you may have already watched for week 4.
It covers the GPD and peaks over threshold at a slower pace than Coles.
The [playlist](https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PL3IxmyGu6qQAOrfzuJU8fGwrZknW0lWJM) and the [slides with speaker notes](https://www.hec.usace.army.mil/confluence/sspdocs/ssptr/class-materials/058-statistical-methods-in-hydrology-april-2025/statistical-methods-in-hydrology-april-2025-course-material) are the same sources as last week.
